name: FENRIS INDUSTRIAL HaulMaster HX-7 Arm
description:
The HaulMaster HX-7 is Fenris Industrial's heavy-labor full-arm replacement, built around a triple-layered steel-composite skeleton with dual-piston hydraulic actuators at the elbow and wrist joints rated for sustained loads of up to 800 kilograms. The modular attachment port at the wrist accepts standardized Fenris industrial tool heads — pneumatic drivers, magnetic clamps, cable-pull winches — swapping in under 30 seconds without tools. The arm is deliberately overbuilt, with 40% structural redundancy so that partial hydraulic failure doesn't strand a worker mid-lift.

The HX-7 is ubiquitous across Great Lakes docks, construction scaffolds, and salvage yards, favored by tier 1-3 laborers who need a limb that works harder than flesh and doesn't require expensive maintenance. Fenris sells directly to labor unions and construction conglomerates in bulk, and the arms are often company-issued — which means the employer technically owns the hardware on your body. Labor rights advocates have made the ownership clause a flashpoint issue in the lower tiers.
installation_requirements: Full shoulder disarticulation, general-practice cyberneural surgeon, reinforced skeletal anchor bolts required at shoulder joint
rejection_risk: Moderate — heavy steel chassis conducts temperature extremes to the shoulder socket; industrial sealant coating reduces but doesn't eliminate rejection risk
maintenance: Monthly hydraulic fluid check, annual piston seal replacement, wrist attachment port cleaning after every shift in corrosive environments
